name: @kruddage/workspace
//version: 0.0.0 is inert and deliberate, not a stale placeholder. version.txt at the repo root is the single source of the released version; introspect.scm stamps it into the WASM build and the shell template, and the site's cache-busting hash derives from what that produces, so routing the number through package.json would put Node in the path of a fact the C build needs. See README.md's 'Versioning and releases' and WORKSPACE.md (Q3).
description: Workspace root for the KRUDD engine. The engine itself still builds through kruddmake, which is not in this workspace; this layer holds the JS packages and the boundaries between them.
//scripts: There is no scripts block and no packageManager field, because there is no package manager left to run them (#1010). The workspace's entry point is `sh tools/workspace/workspace.sh <task>`, which is the same shape as `sh krudd/kruddmake/kruddmake.sh <task>` — two doors, named in the same words (WORKSPACE.md, Q2). Each package still declares its own scripts; workspace.sh reads those back, which is also what lets `check`, `test:native` and `smoke` address a single package without a filter flag.
//test: The workspace's own suite is `sh tools/workspace/workspace.sh test`: every package's own `test` script (engine, site, barriers, render-diff — dawn-smoke has none, it holds no JS). Pure Node, no compiler, no emsdk — and it does not run the native C suite. That is `workspace.sh test:native`, or `sh krudd/kruddmake/run-tests.sh` directly. See WORKSPACE.md (Q2).
//this-file: Kept, though no tool resolves it any more: it is where the version note above lives (WORKSPACE.md, Q3) and it states the Node floor for the whole JS layer. tools/barriers reads the per-package manifests, not this one.
